newsitem.title: UK: EU Commissioner says has no crystal ball on EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU Commissioner says has no crystal ball on EMU.

text.p: European Union monetary affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday he had no "crystal ball" regarding who would qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in the first wave and that he could not make a prediction about Italy's likelihood of doing so.
"For Italy, I can't anticipate the results," de Silguy told journalists. He was in London for a series of meetings with British financial authorities and industry leaders.

"I haven't got a crystal ball. We must wait for the figures for 1997," he said, referring to the economic data which will form the basis of the decision-making process regarding the ins and outs of EMU.
"The qualification (for EMU) is based on a high degree of economic convergence -- it's not a geographical or linguistic criteria," de Silguy said. "I do not want to make a pre-selection."
European Commission official forecasts released late last year showed Italy was expected to have a deficit to GDP ratio of 3.3 percent in 1997, and a debt to GDP ratio of 122.3 percent.

These figures are above the three percent and 60 percent thresholds for qualifying members, although the Maastricht Treaty contains a passage allowing for some consideration if a country is seen to be making sufficient progress.
